---
title: "Optimised Glider II"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# GENERATED, from `_inputs.yml` at the notebook root (rule 34 keeps this cell).
#
# THE BRIEF. True of the whole aircraft, inherited by every chapter and entry,
# and never superseded -- a fork that departs from one of these is not a fork,
# it is a different aircraft and so a different notebook.
#
# Parsed here rather than by `notebook_inputs()` in `_notebook.py`, which does
# exactly this for a chapter. That file is reached through `_model.qmd`, which
# this page does not include and must not: `_notebook.py` imports aerosandbox
# and matplotlib, and the whole point of this page is that it reads source and
# executes none of it. It re-renders on every commit; it costs 10 s because
# nothing here imports a model.
import pathlib
import re

_ROW = re.compile(r"^\s*-\s*[a-z0-9][a-z0-9/-]*\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$")
_brief, _key = {}, None
for _line in pathlib.Path("_inputs.yml").read_text().splitlines():
    if not _line.strip() or _line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
        continue
    _row = _ROW.match(_line)
    if _row and _key:
        _brief[_key].append(_row.group(1).strip('"').strip("'"))
    elif re.match(r"^\w+:\s*$", _line):
        _key = _line.split(":")[0]
        _brief.setdefault(_key, [])
    else:
        _key = None

for _k, _style, _heading in (("specified", "tip", "Initial user specifications"),
                             ("assumed", "note", "Initial assumptions")):
    _rows = _brief.get(_k) or []
    if not _rows:
        continue
    print("::: {.callout-" + _style + "}")
    print(f"## {_heading}\n")
    for _n, _t in enumerate(_rows, 1):
        print(f"{_n}. {_t}")
    print(":::\n")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# GENERATED FROM THE CHAPTERS, never drawn by hand (rule 34 keeps this block).
#
# Reads source, executes none of it: no chapter model is imported or solved. On
# a page that now re-renders after EVERY entry, that property stopped being a
# nicety -- it is what makes the refresh cost 10 s instead of a re-solve.
#
# `create_chapter` deletes this page's freeze when it scaffolds a chapter, and
# `write.py` re-renders it before every commit, because rule 12 cannot protect
# a page that belongs to no chapter. Rule 40 checks that one of them happened.
#
# WHAT THE PICTURE SAYS. A box is a chapter, carrying the change that produced
# it; a tick below it is an entry. A fork puts the child on the SAME RANK as the
# tick it was taken from, so the arrow is horizontal and every line starts level
# with the entry it came from -- which makes y an axis. How far down two lines
# reach is directly comparable, and the lowest tick on the page is the most
# recent work.
#
# Three settings are load-bearing rather than taste:
#   * `ranksep="... equally"` is what makes a chapter's ticks EVENLY spaced. A
#     rank is as tall as the tallest thing in it, so without this a rank holding
#     some other chapter's box stretched one chapter's entry spacing.
#   * the BOX HEIGHT is therefore the entry spacing, since `equally` sizes every
#     rank to the tallest thing in any of them. Tighter entries means smaller
#     boxes, not a smaller `ranksep` -- that has no effect at all.
#   * DECLARATION ORDER is the only lever on which side a fork lands. `dir=back`
#     does nothing (`constraint=false` removes the edge from ordering),
#     `ordering=out` only sorts a node's own out-edges, and `group`/`weight`
#     change nothing measurable. Reversing declaration order mirrors the whole
#     tree, so the side is chosen here -- alternating by generation, so a
#     straight chain zig-zags rather than marching off one edge.
import pathlib
import re

_TITLE = re.compile(r'^title:\s*"(.+)"\s*$', re.M)
_ENTRY = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-")


def _fork(_d):
    """`_fork.yml` as parent, summary and the parent's entry count at the fork."""
    _f = _d / "_fork.yml"
    if not _f.exists():
        return None, "", 0
    _t = _f.read_text()
    _g = lambda _k: (re.search(rf'^{_k}:\s*"?(.+?)"?\s*$', _t, re.M) or [None, ""])[1]
    return (_g("parent") or None), _g("summary"), int(_g("at_entry") or 0)


_chapters = sorted(p for p in pathlib.Path("chapters").iterdir() if p.is_dir())
_ch = {}
for _c in _chapters:
    _index = _c / "index.qmd"
    _m = _TITLE.search(_index.read_text()) if _index.exists() else None
    _p, _s, _at = _fork(_c)
    _ch[_c.name] = dict(
        label=(_s.rstrip(".") or (_m.group(1) if _m else _c.name)),
        # Derived, so it needs no recording and cannot fall out of step: add an
        # entry and the chapter grows a tick.
        total=len([q for q in _c.glob("*.qmd") if _ENTRY.match(q.name)]),
        # Only a parent that still exists: a fork naming a renamed chapter
        # should leave a root node rather than a dangling edge.
        parent=(_p if _p and (pathlib.Path("chapters") / _p).is_dir() else None),
        at=_at)

# Declaration order decides each fork's side; alternate by generation.
_kid_of = {_n: _c["parent"] for _n, _c in _ch.items() if _c["parent"]}
_key = {}


def _walk(_n, _k, _step, _depth):
    _key[_n] = _k
    _sibs = sorted(_m for _m, _c in _ch.items() if _c["parent"] == _n)
    for _i, _kid in enumerate(_sibs):
        _base = -1 if _depth % 2 == 0 else 1
        _walk(_kid, _k + (_base if _i % 2 == 0 else -_base) * _step, _step / 2,
              _depth + 1)


for _r in [_n for _n in _ch if _n not in _kid_of]:
    _walk(_r, 0.0, 1.0, 0)
_seq = sorted(_ch, key=lambda _n: _key.get(_n, 0.0))

print("```{dot}")
# Text size here is fixed and there is no point fighting it. Raising `fontsize`
# widens the diagram in exact proportion -- 11pt gives 7.94in, 13pt gives
# 9.36in, a ratio of 1.18 both ways -- so the page scales it back to the column
# and the glyphs come out the same size. Widening the DISPLAY does change the
# arithmetic, and `column: page` was tried: it renders at 902px instead of 614
# and the type lands near the prose size. It was not an improvement to look at,
# so the diagram sits in the body column like everything else.
print("//| fig-width: 6.4")
print("digraph lineage {")
print('  bgcolor="transparent"; rankdir=TB; nodesep=0.22;')
print('  ranksep="0.05 equally"; splines=spline;')
# The site's own palette, read out of its stylesheet rather than picked. A
# chapter box takes the callout-note blue -- #0d6efd on its own pale ground --
# because a box is both a link and the same kind of object a callout is. The
# ticks take the callout-tip green, so entries read as a different KIND of
# thing from the chapters they hang off rather than as smaller ones. The lines
# are black: they are the structure everything else sits on.
print('  node [shape=box style="rounded,filled" fontname="Helvetica" '
      'fontsize=11 height=0.22 margin="0.2,0.03" penwidth=1.2 '
      'fillcolor="#e7f0ff" color="#0d6efd" fontcolor="#0d6efd"];')
print('  edge [color="#000000" arrowsize=0.55 penwidth=1.2 arrowhead=none];')
for _n in _seq:
    print(f'  "{_n}" [label="{_ch[_n]["label"]}" '
          f'URL="chapters/{_n}/index.html"];')
    for _i in range(1, _ch[_n]["total"] + 1):
        print(f'  "{_n}__e{_i}" [shape=point width=0.055 color="#198754" '
              f'fillcolor="#198754"];')
for _n in _seq:
    _prev = f'"{_n}"'
    for _i in range(1, _ch[_n]["total"] + 1):
        print(f"  {_prev} -> \"{_n}__e{_i}\";")
        _prev = f'"{_n}__e{_i}"'
for _n in _seq:
    _p, _at = _ch[_n]["parent"], _ch[_n]["at"]
    if not _p:
        continue
    # Clamped: a recorded count can outrun the parent if entries were removed,
    # and a fork from an unwritten tick would draw an edge to nothing.
    _at = max(1, min(_at or 1, _ch[_p]["total"]))
    print(f'  {{rank=same; "{_p}__e{_at}"; "{_n}"}}')
    print(f'  "{_p}__e{_at}" -> "{_n}" [constraint=false arrowhead=normal];')
print("}")
print("```")
```
